name: Agriculture
tagline: Crop area, production and yield, mandi arrivals and prices, procurement from farmers, and dairy milk collection with fat and SNF
description: Crop statistics such as India's district-wise area, production and yield (Directorate of Economics & Statistics, data.gov.in), FAOSTAT and USDA NASS extracts and farm plot records; Agmarknet and eNAM mandi arrival and price reports with minimum, maximum and modal prices; MSP procurement registers from state agencies and FCI with farmer payments through PFMS/DBT; and dairy cooperative milk collection data from Automatic Milk Collection Units (AMCU), bulk milk coolers and dairy ERPs with fat, SNF and rate per litre, including Hindi headers written in Latin letters such as mandi, fasal, kisan and doodh.

fields.label: Date
fields.description: When the price was reported, the produce bought or the milk collected; the dashboard's time axis.

fields.label: Crop / agricultural year
fields.description: The year or agricultural year (such as 2019-20) of crop statistics.

fields.label: Area sown / harvested
fields.description: Area under the crop, in hectares or acres; official Indian statistics give it in '000 hectares.

fields.label: Production
fields.description: Crop harvested, in tonnes, quintals or kg ('000 tonnes in official statistics; bales for cotton).

fields.label: Yield (per area)
fields.description: Production per unit of area, such as tonnes per hectare or kg per hectare.

fields.label: Arrivals quantity
fields.description: Produce brought to the market, in tonnes (Agmarknet) or quintals.

fields.label: Modal price
fields.description: The price at which most of the day's produce traded, usually per quintal (100 kg).

fields.label: Farmer
fields.description: One farmer or milk pourer; repeats once per purchase or collection.

fields.label: Quantity procured
fields.description: Produce bought from the farmer, usually in quintals or tonnes.

fields.label: Amount payable / paid
fields.description: Value of the produce or milk bought, payable to the farmer.

fields.label: Milk quantity
fields.description: Milk collected or produced, in litres or kg.

fields.label: Fat %
fields.description: Butterfat content of the milk, in percent (such as 4.2).

fields.label: SNF %
fields.description: Solids-not-fat content of the milk, in percent (such as 8.5).

subDomains.name: Crop area, production & yield
subDomains.description: One row per crop per district or state (or per farm plot) per season and year, with area sown, production and yield.

subDomains.name: Mandi arrivals & prices
subDomains.description: One row per commodity and variety per market per day, with arrivals and minimum, maximum and modal prices (Agmarknet, eNAM).

subDomains.name: Procurement from farmers
subDomains.description: One row per purchase from a farmer at a procurement centre, with crop, quantity, MSP, amount and payment status.

subDomains.name: Dairy milk collection
subDomains.description: One row per farmer per shift (or per animal per day) with milk quantity, fat %, SNF %, rate and amount at a society or collection centre.

kpis.name: Production
kpis.definition: Crop harvested in the period, in the unit of the production column.
kpis.formula: Sum of production
pitfalls: Crops are measured differently (cotton in bales of 170 kg, coconut in nuts), so a total across crops adds unlike units; compare within a crop.

kpis.name: Area sown
kpis.definition: Area under the crops in the period, in the unit of the area column (hectares, acres or '000 ha).
kpis.formula: Sum of area
pitfalls: Adding seasons gives gross cropped area: land sown twice in a year counts twice.

kpis.name: Yield
kpis.definition: Production per unit of area, in the file's units (tonnes per hectare when area is in hectares and production in tonnes).
kpis.formula: Σ production ÷ Σ area, on rows that have both (ratio of totals, not an average of row yields)

variants.label: Area-weighted yield
variants.caveat: No production column, so yield is the yield column averaged with area as weight.

variants.label: Average of yield
variants.caveat: No production or area column, so yield is a simple average of the yield column, not weighted by area.

pitfalls: Comparing yields across crops mixes very different scales (sugarcane about 80 t/ha, pulses under 1 t/ha); compare a crop with itself across districts or years.
Area in '000 hectares and production in '000 tonnes give tonnes per hectare; quintals per hectare are ten times larger.

kpis.name: Irrigated share
kpis.definition: Share of the crop area that is irrigated.
kpis.formula: Σ irrigated area ÷ Σ area, on rows that have both

kpis.name: Crops
kpis.definition: Distinct crops in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct crops

kpis.name: Fertiliser per hectare
kpis.definition: Fertiliser applied per unit of crop area, in the file's units.
kpis.formula: Σ fertiliser ÷ Σ area, on rows that have both
pitfalls: Fertiliser is reported either as product (urea, DAP) or as nutrients (N + P + K); keep one basis.

kpis.name: Pesticide per hectare
kpis.definition: Pesticide applied per unit of crop area, in the file's units.
kpis.formula: Σ pesticide ÷ Σ area, on rows that have both

kpis.name: Average rainfall
kpis.definition: Average rainfall over the rows in the period, in the unit of the rainfall column (usually mm).
kpis.formula: Average of rainfall
pitfalls: Rainfall repeats on every crop row of a district and year, so districts with more crops weigh more.

kpis.name: Arrivals
kpis.definition: Produce brought to the markets in the period, in the unit of the arrivals column (tonnes in Agmarknet).
kpis.formula: Sum of arrivals

kpis.name: Average modal price
kpis.definition: Modal price weighted by arrivals: the typical price per unit traded (per quintal in Agmarknet).
kpis.formula: Σ (modal price × arrivals) ÷ Σ arrivals, on rows that have both

variants.label: Average of modal price
variants.caveat: No arrivals column, so this is a simple average of price reports, not weighted by quantity.

pitfalls: An average across commodities mixes goods priced very differently (onion against cardamom); filter to one commodity and variety first.
Agmarknet prices are per quintal (100 kg); retail prices per kg are 100 times smaller.

kpis.name: Price spread
kpis.definition: How far apart the highest and lowest prices of the day were, relative to the modal price.
kpis.formula: Σ (max price − min price) ÷ Σ modal price, on rows with all three
pitfalls: A wide spread often reflects mixed quality grades on the same day rather than an unstable market.

kpis.name: Markets reporting
kpis.definition: Distinct markets that reported in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct markets

kpis.name: Commodities
kpis.definition: Distinct commodities traded or reported in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct commodities

kpis.name: Average minimum price
kpis.definition: Minimum price weighted by arrivals.
kpis.formula: Σ (min price × arrivals) ÷ Σ arrivals, on rows that have both

variants.label: Average of minimum price
variants.caveat: No arrivals column, so this is a simple average of price reports, not weighted by quantity.

kpis.name: Average maximum price
kpis.definition: Maximum price weighted by arrivals.
kpis.formula: Σ (max price × arrivals) ÷ Σ arrivals, on rows that have both

variants.label: Average of maximum price
variants.caveat: No arrivals column, so this is a simple average of price reports, not weighted by quantity.

kpis.name: Price reports below MSP
kpis.definition: Share of price reports whose modal price was below the minimum support price.
kpis.formula: Reports with modal price < MSP ÷ reports with both
pitfalls: MSP applies to fair average quality (FAQ) produce; lower grades legitimately trade below it.

kpis.name: Quantity procured
kpis.definition: Produce bought from farmers in the period, in the unit of the quantity column (usually quintals or tonnes).
kpis.formula: Sum of quantity procured
pitfalls: Quintals and tonnes differ tenfold (1 tonne = 10 quintals); check the unit before comparing centres or seasons.

kpis.name: Farm procurement value
kpis.definition: Value of produce bought from farmers in the period.
kpis.formula: Sum of amount, or Σ (quantity × MSP)

variants.label: Quantity × MSP
variants.caveat: No amount column, so value = quantity procured × MSP on each row (quantity and MSP must use the same unit, such as quintals).

kpis.name: Farmers
kpis.definition: Distinct farmers who sold produce or poured milk in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct farmers
pitfalls: If farmers are identified by name, two farmers with one name count once and one farmer spelt two ways counts twice.

kpis.name: Quantity per farmer
kpis.definition: Produce bought per farmer in the period.
kpis.formula: Quantity procured ÷ distinct farmers

kpis.name: Farmer payment completion
aliases: Share of value paid to farmers
kpis.definition: Share of the value bought that has been paid to farmers.
kpis.formula: Σ amount with a paid status ÷ Σ amount with any status

variants.label: Paid rows ÷ rows
variants.caveat: No amount column, so each purchase counts once whatever its value.

pitfalls: Rows with no payment status are left out, not counted as unpaid.

kpis.name: Days to pay farmers
kpis.definition: Average days from purchase to payment, for purchases that have been paid.
kpis.formula: Average of (payment date − purchase date) in days

variants.label: Average days from purchase to payment

pitfalls: Only paid rows have a payment date, so unpaid purchases, the longest waits, are left out until they are paid.

kpis.name: Average price paid to farmers
kpis.definition: Value paid per unit of produce bought.
kpis.formula: Σ amount ÷ Σ quantity procured, on rows that have both

kpis.name: Procurement centres
kpis.definition: Distinct procurement centres, societies or collection centres active in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct centres

kpis.name: Average land holding
kpis.definition: Average land holding per farmer, each farmer counted once.
kpis.formula: Average over farmers of each farmer's land holding

kpis.name: Villages covered
kpis.definition: Distinct villages with a purchase or collection in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct villages

kpis.name: Milk collected
kpis.definition: Milk collected or produced in the period, in the unit of the milk column (litres or kg).
kpis.formula: Sum of milk quantity
pitfalls: Litres and kg differ by about 3% (1 litre of milk weighs about 1.03 kg); keep one unit.

kpis.name: Average fat %
kpis.definition: Fat content of the milk collected, weighted by quantity.
kpis.formula: Σ (fat % × quantity) ÷ Σ quantity, on rows with a fat reading

variants.label: Average of fat %
variants.caveat: No milk-quantity column, so this is a simple average of fat readings, not weighted by quantity.

pitfalls: A plain average of fat readings overweights small pourers; the weighted figure is what the dairy actually received.
Buffalo milk runs about 6–8% fat against about 3.5–4.5% for cow milk, so the mix drives the average.

kpis.name: Average SNF %
kpis.definition: Solids-not-fat content of the milk collected, weighted by quantity.
kpis.formula: Σ (SNF % × quantity) ÷ Σ quantity, on rows with an SNF reading

variants.label: Average of SNF %
variants.caveat: No milk-quantity column, so this is a simple average of SNF readings, not weighted by quantity.

kpis.name: Average milk price
kpis.definition: Amount paid per litre (or kg) of milk collected.
kpis.formula: Σ amount ÷ Σ milk quantity, on rows that have both

variants.label: Quantity-weighted rate
variants.caveat: No amount column, so the price is the rate per litre weighted by quantity.

pitfalls: Milk is priced on fat and SNF, so a higher average price can mean richer milk rather than a better rate.

kpis.name: Milk payment
kpis.definition: Amount payable to farmers for the milk collected in the period.
kpis.formula: Sum of amount, or Σ (rate × quantity)

variants.label: Rate × quantity
variants.caveat: No amount column, so payment = rate × quantity on each row.

kpis.name: Milk per farmer
kpis.definition: Milk collected per farmer in the period.
kpis.formula: Milk collected ÷ distinct farmers
pitfalls: Over a month this is milk per farmer for the whole month, not per day.

kpis.name: Milk per animal
kpis.definition: Milk produced per animal recorded in the period.
kpis.formula: Milk ÷ distinct animals
pitfalls: Dry animals with no milk record are left out, so this is milk per animal in milk.

kpis.name: Buffalo milk share
kpis.definition: Share of milk collected that is buffalo milk.
kpis.formula: Buffalo milk ÷ all milk collected

kpis.name: Fat collected (kg)
kpis.definition: Kilograms of butterfat in the milk collected: what two-axis milk pricing pays for.
kpis.formula: Σ (fat % × quantity) ÷ 100
pitfalls: Exact only when quantity is in kg; litres understate kg fat by about 3%.

charts.title: Production by crop and year
charts.reason: Years in order across, crops down: a heatmap shows which crops grew and which shrank without adding unlike units together.

charts.title: Production by crop
charts.reason: One total compared across named crops: sorted horizontal bars keep labels readable. Top 12 plus Others.

charts.title: Area by season
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across a few seasons (kharif, rabi, zaid, whole year): a donut shows how the cropped area splits.

charts.title: Production by state
charts.reason: One total compared across states, with a drill-down to districts: sorted bars, top 15 plus Others.

charts.title: Yield by crop
charts.reason: Yield recomputed per crop from its own production and area, sorted; each crop has its own scale, so read it against the same crop elsewhere.

charts.title: Yield by district
charts.reason: Where the land is most productive: yield recomputed per district, sorted. Filter to one crop first, since crop mix drives yield.

charts.title: Minimum, modal and maximum price
charts.reason: Three prices in one currency on one axis: the band between minimum and maximum shows the day's range around the modal price.

charts.title: Arrivals over time
charts.reason: An additive quantity per period: columns show the harvest glut and lean months.

charts.title: Arrivals by market
charts.reason: Which mandis handle the most produce: sorted bars, top 15 plus Others.

charts.title: Arrivals by commodity
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across many commodities: a treemap sizes each by the quantity that arrived.

charts.title: Modal price by market
charts.reason: Where the same produce fetches more: the modal price per market, sorted. Filter to one commodity first.

charts.title: Price spread by commodity
charts.reason: Which commodities trade at the most uneven prices: the recomputed spread per commodity, sorted.

charts.title: Market summary
charts.reason: Arrivals, price, spread and range of commodities per market side by side in a sortable table.

charts.title: Procurement over time
charts.reason: One additive quantity over continuous time: an area shows how the procurement season builds and tails off.

charts.title: Farmers over time
charts.reason: Distinct farmers per period cannot be added across periods, so they are recomputed for each and drawn as a line.

charts.title: Procurement by centre
charts.reason: Which centres buy the most: sorted bars, top 15 plus Others.

charts.title: Procurement by crop
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across a few crops: a donut shows what was bought.

charts.title: Value by payment status
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across a few payment states: a donut shows how much of the value is still unpaid.

charts.title: Days to pay farmers by centre
charts.reason: Where farmers wait longest to be paid: average days from purchase to payment per centre, sorted, centres under 20 rows hidden.

charts.title: Farmers by quantity sold
charts.reason: How purchases are spread: farmers per band of quantity show whether small or large growers dominate.

charts.title: Centre scorecard
charts.reason: Quantity, farmers, value and payment per centre side by side in a sortable table.

charts.title: Milk collected over time
charts.reason: One additive quantity over continuous time: an area shows the flush and lean seasons.

charts.title: Fat and SNF over time
charts.reason: Two weighted percentages on one scale: lines show whether milk quality moves with the season.

charts.title: Milk by shift
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across morning and evening collections: a donut shows the split.

charts.title: Milk by society or centre
charts.reason: Which societies or collection centres bring in the most milk: sorted bars, top 15 plus Others.

charts.title: Milk by animal type
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across cow, buffalo and mixed milk: a donut shows the mix that drives fat and price.

charts.title: Fat % by society or centre
charts.reason: Where milk is richest or thinnest: quantity-weighted fat per centre, sorted, centres under 30 rows hidden.

charts.title: Farmers by milk poured
charts.reason: How collections are spread: farmers per band of milk poured show how many small pourers the society serves.

charts.title: Society scorecard
charts.reason: Milk, pourers, quality and price per society side by side in a sortable table.

pitfalls: Units differ between sources: tonnes, quintals (100 kg) and kg; hectares, acres and '000 hectares; litres and kg of milk. Check them before comparing files or crops.
Yield, prices, fat and SNF are recomputed from totals (production ÷ area, quantity-weighted averages) for every period and group; never average row-level figures.
Crops, commodities and milk types are not interchangeable: an average price or yield across them reflects the mix more than performance, so filter to one first.
Agricultural years and seasons (kharif, rabi) cross calendar years; an agricultural year such as 2019-20 runs from July to June.
Market prices are reported per day and market; days without trading are missing, not zero.
